dish: Hainanese chicken rice — steamed or crispy-skin roast chicken, rice cooked in garlicky chicken stock
w: Balestier's other chicken-rice institution (alongside Boon Tong Kee): founded in 1953 by Hainanese immigrants and run by three generations, everything made from scratch — silky steamed or crisp-skinned roast chicken over fluffy rice cooked in garlicky chicken broth, with chilli, dark soy and ginger paste. The Loy Kee Special Set is the full Hainanese spread on one tray.

dish: Tau sar piah (flaky mung-bean pastry), sweet and salty
w: Balestier is Singapore's tau sar piah street, and Loong Fatt (since 1948) is its original — still in the same shophouse with the old tiled walls and floor, wooden tables and booths, baking flaky mung-bean pastries by hand. A stop on the National Heritage Board's Balestier Food Trail.

dish: Beef hor fun in black-bean gravy with wok hei; prawn paste chicken
address: 1 Thomson Road, #01-326, Balestier Hill Shopping Centre, Singapore 320002
w: A long-running zi char stall in the corner of a Balestier Hill coffeeshop, famous for its beef hor fun — silky rice-noodle sheets and tender beef in a fragrant black-bean gravy loaded with wok hei — the subject of Dr Leslie Tay's 'beef hor fun challenge'. Prawn paste chicken is the other order. Reviewers note consistency depends on who is at the wok.

dish: Rojak in a thick assam–hae ko sauce with jellyfish and century egg
address: Whampoa Makan Place, 90 Whampoa Drive, #01-06, Singapore 320090
w: The long-famous Balestier rojak, now at Whampoa Food Centre and a repeat Michelin Bib Gourmand pick — a killer sauce of assam, fermented prawn paste and sugar tossed with crunchy jellyfish and creamy century egg alongside the usual fruit, you tiao and tau pok.

dish: Wet-style fried Hokkien prawn mee with thick bee hoon
address: Whampoa Makan Place, 90 Whampoa Drive, #01-32, Singapore 320090
w: You see the queue before the stall: a Michelin Bib Gourmand (2023) fried Hokkien mee that pairs thick bee hoon with yellow noodles in a slightly wet, umami-laden prawn stock. Open from mid-afternoon into the small hours, it is Whampoa's night-market anchor.

dish: Sliced and fried fish-head bee hoon in milky fish stock
n: Beach Road Fish Head Bee Hoon
address: Whampoa Makan Place, 91 Whampoa Drive, #01-46, Singapore
w: Held the Michelin Bib Gourmand in 2024 and 2025, and widely called one of Singapore's best fish soups: sliced or fried fish-head bee hoon in a rich, milky stock finished with fried garlic. Morning hours only, a few days a week — go early.

dish: Braised soy duck rice and Cantonese duck porridge
address: Whampoa Makan Place, 90 Whampoa Drive, #01-07, Singapore 320090
w: A former Michelin Bib Gourmand (2017) braised-duck stall: soy duck rice drenched in gravy, but regulars come for the velvety Cantonese-style duck porridge with a splash of braising gravy — 'you have never tasted duck porridge this good' (Miss Tam Chiak).

dish: Orh luak (fried oyster omelette) with citrusy homemade chilli
address: Whampoa Makan Place, Whampoa Drive, Singapore — stall unit to confirm at geocode
w: A one-dish Michelin-recognised stall: orh luak with just the right balance of egg and gooey starch, fried to crisp brown edges and served with a citrusy homemade chilli.

dish: Handmade ban mian with prawns, clams, sliced fish, fish maw or pig's kidney
address: Whampoa Makan Place, 91 Whampoa Drive, Singapore — stall unit to confirm at geocode
w: A well-known Block 91 morning-market stall for handmade ban mian and noodle soups, loaded up with prawns, abalone clams, sliced fish, fish maw or pig's kidneys.

n: Mat Noh & Rose Authentic Ginger Fried Chicken Rice
address: Whampoa Makan Place, Whampoa Drive, #01-27, Singapore
w: A Muslim-owned stall tucked into a far corner of Whampoa Makan Place that has achieved 'main character status' for one dish — crisp ginger-marinated fried chicken over rice.

dish: Lor mee with ngoh hiang, fish nuggets and braised pork
n: Amoy St Lor Mee (Best Lu Mian In Town)
address: Whampoa Makan Place, 91 Whampoa Drive, #01-19, Singapore
w: Whampoa is almost synonymous with this stall and its bold claim to the 'Best Lu Mian In Town': a two-item menu of thick, starchy lor mee laden with ngoh hiang, fish nuggets and braised pork (or the amped-up Jumbo Meal), with long morning queues.

dish: Teochew fishball noodles by morning, fish-head steamboat by night
n: Xin Heng Feng Guo Tiao Tan
address: Whampoa Makan Place, 91 Whampoa Drive, #01-14/15, Singapore
w: A breakfast stalwart serving fishball kway teow and mee pok from 5am, switching to fish-head steamboat in the evening.

dish: Chai tow kway (fried carrot cake), white or black
address: Whampoa Makan Place, Whampoa Drive, #01-34, Singapore
w: A carrot-cake stall carrying the Tanglin Halt name to Whampoa — picked by both Seth Lui's and Daniel Food Diary's Whampoa round-ups among the market's worth-queuing stalls.
